metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Dealing with mild hamstring strain
metadata.description: McCaffrey is dealing with a mild hamstring strain rather than a quadriceps injury, and the 49ers believe he'll be ready following the team's Week 8 bye, David Lombardi of SF Standard reports.
metadata.analysis: After McCaffrey briefly exited Sunday's loss to Atlanta with what had been described as a thigh issue, this update offers more clarity on the injury and a favorable outlook. The timing of the 49ers' bye gives the veteran running back added recovery time ahead of their next game in Week 9 versus the Raiders, though his practice status will still be worth monitoring once San Francisco returns to work. Kaelon Black will be a priority add off waivers considering CMC's injury history.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey has Mild Hamstring Strain, Should be Ready for Week 9
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) ended up having a mild hamstring strain in Sunday's Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons, not a quadriceps injury, according to David Lombardi of The San Francisco Standard. The 49ers think McCaffrey will be ready to go after their Week 8 bye in Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders. CMC left the game and was seen running to the locker room with a trainer before eventually returning to the contest for the 49ers. The 30-year-old four-time Pro Bowler and three-time first-team All-Pro handled a season-low seven carries against Atlanta while missing valuable time, but he managed to find the end zone for the sixth straight game on 39 rushing yards while adding six catches for 61 yards through the air. We will be keeping a close eye on McCaffrey's practice status next week as the team prepares for the Raiders, but as long as CMC is on track to play, he will be a must-start in all fantasy formats. Through seven weeks, he has 84 carries for 389 yards (4.6 yards per carry) with a league-high eight rushing touchdowns. McCaffrey has added 34 receptions on 42 targets for 251 yards through the air.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Not Worried About "Thigh" Injury
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey (thigh) is not worried about his injury. McCaffrey suffered a thigh injury on the second drive of the game. He returned but had only four touches after the injury. McCaffrey said his leg "just died on me. I was just trying to keep it warm and not make it worse, but there's only so much you can do to get back to where you want to be. I'll be fine. I know that. I'll be all right." He was dominating early, totaling 69 yards and a touchdown on the first drive alone. With the 49ers on bye for Week 8, McCaffrey will have time to heal before facing the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 9. While fantasy managers shouldn't sound alarms yet, McCaffrey's thigh injury is concerning given the star running back's injury history.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey's Rushing Volume Hindered by Brief Exit
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey totaled nine carries, 39 rushing yards, and one rushing touchdown during Sunday's Week 7 loss against the Atlanta Falcons. He also caught six of seven targets for an additional 61 receiving yards. McCaffrey had a very productive day when he was on the field, but his rushing volume was limited by a mix of injury and game script. The 30-year-old missed a portion of the game with a thigh injury, and it was serious enough that he had to go to the locker room for evaluation and was listed as questionable. He did end up returning, although the Niners used him in the passing game more than the rushing attack since they were trailing Atlanta. San Francisco went on to lose, but McCaffrey salvaged his performance (especially in PPR leagues) with the six catches, 100 scrimmage yards, and one touchdown. As long as he's healthy, he remains a high-end RB1 on the other side of his Week 8 bye.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey gains 100 yards, scores in Week 7 loss
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey rushed for 39 yards and a touchdown on seven carries, adding six receptions for 61 yards in Sunday's 29-20 loss to the Falcons.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey dealt with a thigh injury for a portion of Sunday's game, but he still ended up gaining 100 yards of offense on 13 touches. He also found the end zone on the ground for the eighth time this season. He remains a top-shelf fantasy option.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Navigates injury in Week 7 loss
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed seven times for 39 yards and a touchdown and brought in six of seven targets for 61 yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey missed the entirety of the second quarter while dealing with a thigh injury, and although he was able to return and play the second half, he finished with his fewest rush attempts and rushing yardage totals of the season. McCaffrey did punch in a one-yard touchdown run that capped off the opening possession of the game, and his work as a receiver, which included a season-high receiving yardage tally, helped prop up his final fantasy line as well. McCaffrey will now have the benefit of the Week 8 bye to heal up before returning to action in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Reenters Sunday's game
metadata.description: McCaffrey (thigh) returned to Sunday's contest in Atlanta, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey missed the entire second quarter as he had his left thigh worked on, which officially left him as questionable to return before he checked back in for the 49ers' first possession of the third quarter. Now that he's back in the contest, he likely will continue to lead San Francisco's backfield.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (thigh) returns to the game
metadata.description: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey (thigh) has returned to the game against the Falcons.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey suffered a thigh injury in the first half and was listed as questionable to return. The broadcast showed that he was on the sideline working before the start of the half and returned on the team's first series.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Goes to locker room Sunday
metadata.description: McCaffrey (thigh) went to the locker room during Sunday's game in Atlanta, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey remained on the sideline for the 49ers' third possession to get his left leg worked on, which seemingly stemmed from a hit he took on a 24-yard catch on the team's first drive. Officially questionable to return due to a thigh injury, he attempted to warm up on San Francisco's bench before jogging to the locker room in the middle of the second quarter. Kaelon Black will be the team's leading runner for as long as McCaffrey is out of the contest.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (thigh) questionable to return
metadata.description: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey (thigh) is questionable to return against the Falcons.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey was seen testing his injured calf on the sideline before running into the locker room. Kaelon Black will serve as the primary running back if McCaffrey is unable to return.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Questionable to return Sunday
metadata.description: McCaffrey (thigh) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest in Atlanta, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey appeared to take a big hit at the end of a 24-yard catch on the 49ers' first drive, but he continued to play through it until the team's third possession, when he stayed on the sideline to get worked on by the training staff. During McCaffrey's absence from the contest, rookie Kaelon Black will be San Francisco's primary running back.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Exits with apparent leg injury
metadata.description: McCaffrey was getting his lower left leg worked on during the first half of Sunday's game in Atlanta, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey took a big hit on the 49ers' first possession of Week 7 action after a 24-yard catch, but he continued to play through it until the team's third drive, when he remained on the sideline to get worked on. For as long as McCaffrey is sidelined, Kaelon Black will be San Francisco's primary RB.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Returns From Thigh Injury Against Falcons
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey (thigh) returned for the team's opening offensive possession of the third quarter against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, according to ESPN's Nick Wagoner, which cuts into the likelihood of rookie Kaelon Black handling the lead role throughout the second half. McCaffrey was initially questionable to return after receiving treatment in the medical tent and on the sideline before heading to the locker room. He recorded four carries for 29 yards and a touchdown, along with three receptions for 45 yards, before his departure. Black took on additional work in his absence and scored on a 30-yard touchdown run, but McCaffrey is back in San Francisco's backfield rotation.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Heads to Locker Room With Thigh Injury
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey (thigh) has headed to the locker room during Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, according to ESPN's Nick Wagoner, which puts rookie Kaelon Black in line for an expanded workload if McCaffrey cannot return. McCaffrey initially received treatment in the medical tent before returning to the sideline, where trainers continued working on his thigh. He remains questionable to return after recording four carries for 29 yards and a touchdown, along with three receptions for 45 yards. Black has taken over backfield duties during McCaffrey's absence and already delivered a 30-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, demonstrating he can handle additional carries against Atlanta.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Questionable to Return with Thigh Injury
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey (thigh) is questionable to return to a Week 7 game against the Atlanta Falcons with a thigh injury, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN. Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reported that McCaffrey was spotted in the medical tent with a massage gun on his left hamstring/thigh. McCaffrey recorded four rushes for 29 yards (7.3 yards per carry) and a touchdown, along with three receptions for 45 yards (15.0 yards per catch), before exiting the contest. While McCaffrey is out, the 49ers will rely on running back Kaelon Black, who has already recorded a 30-yard touchdown run.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Should See More Receiving Work In Week 7
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey had his biggest game of the season in Week 6 against the Commanders. McCaffrey gained 118 scrimmage yards, extended his scoring streak to a fifth game with two touchdown runs, and logged 25 touches - his most in a game all year. McCaffrey led the team with nine catches and 10 targets with Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) out of the lineup and Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) forced out early due to injury. Both wide receivers will be out for Week 7, which puts McCaffrey in position to act as Brock Purdy's primary target. The Atlanta Falcons are tied for the fourth most receptions allowed to opposing running backs through Week 6. McCaffrey has four top-10 finishes under his belt already in 2026, and is projected for another one in Week 7. He should be locked into starting lineups.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey scores two TDs in Week 6
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey carried the ball 16 times for 64 yards and two touchdowns while catching nine of his 10 targets for 53 yards in a 23-17 win over the Commanders in Week 6's Monday night game. He also lost a fumble in the contest.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey turned in a huge performance in the close win. He scored his touchdowns on a pair of one-yard runs in the first half, while he led the 49ers in targets and receptions. With seven total touchdowns through his first six games this year, the veteran tailback will be a top-three fantasy option heading into Week 7's road matchup vs. the Falcons.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Two touchdowns in Week 6 win
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two touchdowns and brought in nine of 10 targets for 53 yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night. He also lost a fumble.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey, who's been subject to a markedly lighter workload than usual over the first weeks of the campaign, recorded season highs in rush attempts, receptions, receiving yards and targets on a very busy night. The star running back also contributed his second multi-touchdown tally of the season, powering into the end zone on a pair of one-yard runs in the first half. McCaffrey logged twice as many carries and nine more targets than rookie backfield mate Kaelon Black, so there's no question who the leader of the ground attack is heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Could See More Receiving Work Amid WR Injuries
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey had 68 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries and three catches for 15 receiving yards on five targets last week. In Week 6, the 49ers face the Commanders, who have been surprisingly effective against the run. Washington has allowed just two rushing touchdowns, the sixth-fewest rushing yards, and the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs in 2026. McCaffrey's utility as a receiver will keep him in play as a top option at his position. The Commanders are in the middle of the pack defending against passes to running backs, and Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) has been ruled out, and Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is questionable, which means more targets could come CMC's way. McCaffrey projects as an RB1 and should be started in fantasy football in Week 6.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (rest) absent from practice Thursday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey (rest) was absent from practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Thursday was San Francisco's first practice of the week, so to no surprise, they gave McCaffrey the day off as a veteran rest day. He should be back on Friday and is expected to be a full go for Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone Sunday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey ran for 68 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries in the 49ers 32-29 win over the Seahawks on Sunday. He also caught 3-of-3 targets for 15 yards receiving.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey continues to find the end zone to make up for his lack of yardage on the season. He scored right after a fumble by Emanuel Wilson this week. He remains an RB1 for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Stretches TD streak to four games
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 11 times for 68 yards and a touchdown while catching all three of his targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey gave the 49ers a 14-10 lead with an 11-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. His 14 touches tied a season low, and McCaffrey has yet to reach 20 touches in a game, as the undefeated 49ers have been content to manage his workload to some extent in order to keep the star running back fresh after McCaffrey averaged over 24 touches per game in the 2025 regular season. The reduced workload hasn't kept McCaffrey from scoring five touchdowns across his last four games, and he'll look to extend his four-game scoring streak in Week 6 against the Commanders.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Can Extend TD Streak To Fourth Game On Sunday
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey was held out of the end zone in Week 1 but has scored at least one touchdown in each of his last three games. Going back to 2025, McCaffrey has scored in 15 of the 49ers' last 21 games. Extending his current touchdown streak against the Seahawks in Week 5 will be difficult, but not impossible. McCaffrey's 15 touches inside the 20 rank 15th among all NFL players and represent a 35% team share in red zone opportunities. He should see another handful of chances to punch one in on Sunday. McCaffrey's talents as a receiver will be in play on Sunday, as the Seahawks have allowed the fourth-most receptions to running backs in 2026, whereas they have given up the lowest success rate on rushing attempts. CMC has his work cut out for him in Week 5, but he is an integral part of the 49ers' offense and can still be counted on for RB1 production.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey scores touchdown in win Sunday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 52 yards and a touchdown while catching three of his five targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey didn't have his biggest day from a yardage standpoint, but he found the end zone on a one-yard run in the fourth quarter. He finished with 18 touches and remains the clear lead back in San Francisco. McCaffrey remains a must-start option heading into Week 5 against Seattle.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Logs 18 touches in close win
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 52 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of five targets for 18 yards in the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey saw a reduced workload by his lofty standards, although he still outpaced backfield mate Kaelon Black by nine carries. The star back had to tough out the majority of his gains on the ground, including his one-yard touchdown run with just under nine minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. McCaffrey has yet to top 15 carries in any game this season, but he has four rushing TDs and 340 total yards heading into a Week 5 road showdown against the Seahawks next Sunday.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Matches Up Well Against Broncos
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is in line for a productive Week 4 when he squares off against the Denver Broncos. So far in 2026, Denver has given up the third-most rushing yards, has the highest EPA allowed per run, and has the most missed tackles in the league. The Broncos defense will also be missing linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hamstring). This makes for an inviting matchup for McCaffrey, who owns the league's fifth-best rushing success rate and the highest average rushing yards before contact among starting running backs. As usual, McCaffrey can be expected to be one of quarterback Brock Purdy's favorite targets. And with Mike Evans (ribs) questionable and expected to be a game-time decision on Sunday, McCaffrey could see his receiving work increase. The Broncos gave up six catches for 70 yards to Kyren Williams last week. McCaffrey is projected as the overall RB6 in Week 4.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone Sunday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey ran for 75 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. He also caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards receiving.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey took over as the clear lead back on Sunday. He found the end zone in the fourth quarter as the Cardinals were making a comeback. He remains a strong RB1 moving forward.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Records 116 total yards in win
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 75 yards and a touchdown while bringing in four of five targets for 41 yards in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey's carry total was modest by his standards, but he still outpaced backup Kaelon Black by 11 rushes and four targets while also recording a one-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter. McCaffrey was highly efficient with his rushing opportunities, and he finished second in receptions and third in targets for the 49ers on the afternoon. San Francisco's pass-catching corps suffered further attrition this weekend -- Mike Evans exited the game with a rib/oblique injury, while Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Saturday -- so McCaffrey could continue to see his receiving work creep up in a Week 4 home showdown against the Broncos next Sunday.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Set for Bounce-Back Week vs. Cardinals
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has the opportunity to bounce back when his team hosts the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3. The star back was part of a large contingent of players who didn't participate in Wednesday's practice but returned on Thursday to prepare for Sunday's divisional matchup. McCaffrey was held to 23 yards on 10 carries in Week 2 but scored two rushing TDs in a convincing 35-13 win against the Miami Dolphins. Arizona has struggled to contain the run early in the 2026 campaign, allowing 243 yards and one touchdown on the ground through two games. CMC should be able to exploit the Cardinals' defense, setting the table for a strong Week 3 across fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey was given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day, which is normal for him at the first practice of the week. He should be a full go for Sunday's game and remains a must-start fantasy option in all league formats for as long as he stays healthy and on the field.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone twice in Week 2
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey gained 23 yards on 10 carries and 43 yards on four catches, scoring twice on the ground in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Week 2, but McCaffrey did score a pair of one-yard plunges. As usual, the dual-threat back was also active in the passing game. McCaffrey is up to 29 total touches through two games, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and 7.0 yards per reception. The 49ers appear to be capping the 30-year-old's usage a bit, but he's still a clear RB1, particularly in PPR formats, when healthy.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Keeps a Useful Role Behind Starting RB
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black remains a strong Week 3 waiver target despite a quieter showing against Miami. Black carried seven times for 25 yards after handling 14 carries for 65 yards in the opener, and he played roughly one-third of the offensive snaps Sunday. Christian McCaffrey remains the clear lead back and handled both goal-line touchdowns, so Black's standalone value is still somewhat dependent on game script. Even so, San Francisco has given the rookie 21 carries through two games, which is enough to make his role worth taking seriously. RotoBaller currently recommends adding Black in 10-team leagues and deeper, viewing him as one of fantasy's better handcuffs with some standalone appeal. He does not need to be forced into lineups every week, but the combination of regular rushing work and the upside he would carry if McCaffrey missed time makes Black a worthwhile waiver add rather than a bench-only lottery ticket.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Scores twice to reach 100 career TDs
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 10 times for 23 yards and two touchdowns while catching both of his targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey opened the scoring with a one-yard touchdown run in the first quarter and added another one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. The two-touchdown performance brought McCaffrey's career regular-season touchdown total up to 100. Exactly half of those touchdowns have come with the 49ers, as McCaffrey joins Marshall Faulk and Randy Moss as the only players to score at least 50 touchdowns apiece for multiple teams, per ESPN Insights. McCaffrey should continue to contribute as both a runner and a pass catcher in Week 3 against the Cardinals.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey In Line For RB1 Performance In Favorable Matchup
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey had 68 rushing yards on 10 carries and converted eight targets into five catches for 20 receiving yards in last week's win over the Rams. His modest output in that game resulted from the 49ers' overall dominance and the effectiveness of backup Kaelon Black (groin), who had 14 carries of his own. With San Francisco heavily favored against the Dolphins in Week 2, there will be less of a need for McCaffrey to produce. However, Black was nursing groin tightness in practices this week and is listed as questionable for Sunday. Restrictions on Black may increase McCaffrey's workload, or open the door for backup Jordan James to get involved. Regardless, McCaffrey's status in San Francisco's offense and his effectiveness when on the field keep him in contention for a top-five finish. As in any week when McCaffrey is healthy, he is a must-start.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (rest) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey (rest) returned to practice for the 49ers as a full participant on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, McCaffrey returns to being a full participant at practice on Thursday after being given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day. He should be good to go for Week 2 and is primed for a huge workload against the Dolphins, especially now that Kaelon Black (groin) has been added to the injury report for the 49ers.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey was a non-participant at San Francisco's practice on Wednesday. The team gave him a routine rest day and he should be back on Thursday, so fantasy managers should have no concerns about him heading into a great Week 2 matchup against the Dolphins.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Played Through Cramping in Season-Opening Win
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said that running back Christian McCaffrey dealt with some cramps during the season-opening win on Thursday over the division-rival Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, but made it through fine, according to ESPN's Nick Wagoner. McCaffrey did not have a huge Week 1 performance, but he did enough to help the Niners pull off a blowout win over a Rams defense that came into the 2026 season expected to be one of the best units in the league. The 30-year-old had 10 carries for 68 yards and caught five of his eight targets for 20 yards. It was a notable reduction in his workload after finishing as the RB1 in fantasy in 2025 with a career- and league-high 413 touches in 17 regular-season starts. Rookie Kaelon Black actually had four more carries than CMC, who did not do much in training camp due to undisclosed tightness. McCaffrey might not see as hefty a workload in 2026, but if he stays healthy again all year, he still has the potential to be a league-winner in San Fran's offense. He is a must-start for a Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey racks up 88 scrimmage yards in win
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey ran 10 times for 68 yards and caught five of eight targets for 20 yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey surprisingly had a split backfield with Kaelon Black, at least much more than expected. The veteran tied Black in touches, 15 to 15, but had the edge in opportunities, 18 to 15, thanks to receiving. It will be interesting to see if this is a Week 1 fluke or a recurring theme, as Black was involved throughout the game, not just when the game was well in hand. Still, CMC is a top-tier asset, and while today was fine, bigger days are ahead.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Efficient with modest workload
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 10 times for 68 yards and brought in five of eight targets for 20 yards during the 49ers' 27-7 Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
metadata.analysis: Coming off a 2025 regular season where he was able to suit up for all 17 games while handling 413 total touches, McCaffrey saw a notable workload reduction to open the new campaign. Rookie third-round pick Kaelon Black actually outpaced McCaffrey by four carries, but it was the latter who edged out his new backfield mate for the team lead in rushing yards. McCaffrey flashed his trademark explosiveness when carrying the ball and should still helm the ground attack on the majority of weeks, although lopsided game scripts in either direction could lead to head coach Kyle Shanahan taking the opportunity to curtail his star running back's volume. McCaffrey will next take aim at what is expected to be a vulnerable Dolphins defense in a Week 2 matchup on Sunday, Sept. 20.
